subject: Vector surge forecast & network policing for private GPU pool
messages:
From: acme.ops@acme-corp.com
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-19 09:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Private pool questions — forecast & policing

Hi Sofia,

We're kicking off prep for a mid-June pilot (50k QPS token-equivalent peak) and need to align on two things quickly:

1) Vector/embedding surge headroom: we expect an inbound burst pattern where our batch/embedding requests double for ~45s every 10 minutes during peak hours. We need sizing guidance (per-GPU qps/embedding throughput assumptions and warmup strategy) so our infra team can provision network and IOPS.

2) Network policing / egress enforcement: our networking team must implement a policing policy (DSCP and rate-limits) at the VPC border. They asked for recommended policing thresholds, burst windows, and QoS markings so they can test with their load generator.

Can your team produce a short runbook and a rough projection for runway (warm pool sizing + admission control curve) we can use in procurement discussions?

Thanks —
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Ops
acme.ops@acme-corp.com
(Attachment: none)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-19 11:23 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector surge forecast & network policing for private GPU pool

Alex —

Thanks for the note. We can put together a short operational runbook and a sizing projection this week. High-level answers to unblock your networking and capacity folks immediately:

- Throughput assumptions (baseline): 1 A100-80GB equiv handles ~1.2k 768-dim embedding ops/sec in continuous mode with batching; for 4096-dim embeddings assume ~350-420 ops/sec depending on quantization.
- Burst model: plan for 2.5x short bursts (30-60s) above sustained QPS. Warm-pool of N GPUs sized to absorb one burst without reallocation (~burst_capacity = target_peak / 1.2k, rounded up).
- Warmup: pre-warm KV cache with a 10–15 minute rolling warmup window for top prefixes; we provide a warmup checklist (attached).
- Network policing: suggest DSCP EF for control/low-latency RPC (model control plane), CS5 for streaming tokens, and a per-flow token-bucket of burst=100MB, sustained=20MB/s per customer flow as a starting point for pilot. Fine-tune with the load generator.

I'm attaching a first-pass runway spreadsheet and a network policing diagram — we'll iterate on numbers with Jonas and Grace and push a consolidated MA plan by Friday.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
(Attachments: runway_projection_v1.xlsx; network_policing_diagram.png; warmup-and-admission-checklist.md)

Date: 2026-04-20 08:47 -07:00
Subject: RE: Vector surge forecast & network policing for private GPU pool

Sofia / Grace — quick internal sanity checks on the assumptions before we finalize:

- Embedding throughput: Sofia's 1.2k/sec for 768-dim seems right for quantized kernels with continuous batching. For safety during bursts we should conservatively use 900/sec per A100-equivalent (to account for jitter, shorter batch windows, and occasional LLAMA2-style attention cost increases).

- Warm pool sizing math (proposal): target pilot peak = 50k token-embedding-equivalent/s; use 900/sec baseline -> need ceil(50_000 / 900) = 56 GPUs to absorb peak if all requests synchronous. With prefix caching and multiplexing we can reduce to ~42 GPUs effective. Recommend starting pilot with 50 GPUs + autoscale headroom of 15% (burst carve-out).

- Admission & policing: network token-buckets should be applied at the VPC border per flow and a second stage at the host interface. Burst window = 60s with leaky-bucket refill tuned to sustained target. For QoS: use DSCP EF for callbacks, CS6 for inference traffic we want prioritized; mark best-effort for non-real-time bulk embeddings.

- Egress: confirm DataCenterCo's egress shaping; if they cap per-customer egress < 1Gbps we'll need to spread fleet across AZs and possibly throttle token rate.

I'll update Sofia's spreadsheet to include the conservative numbers and a short sensitivity table. Grace, can you validate the warmup checklist durations (10–15 min) vs our observed cache cold-start in staging?

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-21 14:12 -07:00
Subject: RE: Vector surge forecast & network policing for private GPU pool

Quick notes from load-test and ops perspective:

- Warmup verification: in last sim we saw 12–18 minutes to reach 90% KV hit rate for top-200 prefixes with a 5% random sample traffic pattern. I'll propose 20 minutes in the checklist for pilot to be conservative and include a rolling pre-warm job that touches the top N embeddings.

- Host-level policing: recommend tc qdisc on host NVMe network interface with fq_codel + HTB classes: class-default (sustained), burst-class (short 60s) and control-class (very low latency). We'll provide tc commands in the runbook.

- Observability: add a per-flow token-drop metric and a rolling 1-min p95 latency for embedding ops to the Console dashboard. Set an alert at 5% token-drop or p95 > 250ms.

I'll review Jonas' conservative GPU counts and sanity-check memory/IO requirements for 50 GPUs and 15% headroom.

Grace
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Final: Pilot runway + network policing plan (action items)

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the consolidated pilot-runway workbook (runway_projection_v2.xlsx), the policing diagram with DSCP/HTB classes (network_policing_diagram.png), and a short warmup & admission checklist we validated in staging. Highlights / decisions we made for pilot:

- Pilot sizing: provision 50 GPUs (A100-equivalent) in the warm pool, with autoscale buffer of 15% and a conservative capacity assumption of 900 embedding ops/sec per GPU for burst planning.
- Warmup: rolling pre-warm job, 20-minute conservative window to reach ~90% KV hit rate for top prefixes.
- Policing: two-tier policing — VPC border token-bucket (burst window 60s, sustained 20MB/s per flow) + host tc qdisc classes. QoS markings: DSCP EF for control, CS6 for prioritized inference streams, BE for bulk batches.
- Observability & alerts: set per-flow drop rate alert (>=5%) and p95 latency alert (>=250ms).

Action items:
- Acme: provision 50 GPUs in the pilot availability zone and deploy test harness that reproduces the 45s/10m burst pattern (Dan at DataCenterCo will help).
- DataCenterCo: confirm egress shaping is set to >=1.5Gbps per customer AZ or provide recommended mitigation if lower.
- Redwood: we'll hand over the runbook and a short tc command snippet; we'll run a joint load-test next Wed and iterate.

Links: Pilot workbook & diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xy-Runway-VectorSurge | HubSpot: HS-872134

I'll loop in Sales/Legal for any procurement sizing notes after your confirmation. Please reply with a thumbs-up or scheduling availability for next Wed's load test.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
